60.head: perf/native-plasticity-20261106
60.body:
Native plasticity and memory retention repeatedly sort the registry and allocate outbound synapse slices. Use canonical node addresses through a stable transient traversal index, remove temporary outbound lists, restrict local prediction-error work to participating sources, and reuse activation order within each propagation cycle.

The first random-map traversal candidate regressed latency and was not merged. The final candidate preserves locality with an address-only index. All registry membership write paths are append-only; cardinality invalidates the index, restore constructs a fresh registry, and Nodes returns a separate slice. No weights or persistent knowledge are duplicated. Growth, concurrent traversal, caller slice isolation and restore are tested.

Final sequential ABBA benchmark, identical Go1.23.2/8-core synthetic workloads, 100 samples/cell: at 40k neurons/160k synapses with nine active units, thought p50 45.245→17.595 ms, p95 58.830→23.945 ms (2.46x), p99 65.635→25.705 ms. Per sensor+thought pair: 12.188→3.835 MB (-68.54%), 561270→1110 allocations (-99.80%). With durable WAL p95 68.890→24.235 ms (2.84x). The 3x large-workload research target was not reached; global activity/retention scans remain. Smaller/dense/lazy/controller and persistence measurements are separately reported, without claiming equivalent workloads.

Frozen d7cb140 reference laws produce identical full canonical bytes after 100 mixed transitions under both legacy and local dynamics. Full local tests, vet/build, registry race tests and existing native regression/recovery checks pass. PR CI 42250379183 and push CI 42250372648 both passed on exact head 87fc532c3d14fb0e9b7ee37523ad308aba503de3. Merged as 32df59b9285d829ae73429c7f277621e63de7ce3 after both workflows succeeded. No schema, numerical law or production policy changes.

Detailed reproducible audit and measurements: https://github.com/mpsprintit-spec/horizon-artificial-brain/blob/0ef994a1d8842b36dbc6b994ecafcb0bf9951174/docs/research/native_foundation/PERFORMANCE.md . Native controller work is in draft #61 and is NOT approved by this optimization: its transfer and causal-credit gates fail.

61.head: research/native-neural-foundation-20261106
61.body:
This opt-in Go experiment lets one canonical Brain select propagate/focus/relax/stop from its current activation, retain the resulting state, and update canonical action-value synapses from observed delayed outcomes. It adds bounded preflight/commit operations, stochastic training versus greedy evaluation, single-use outcome provenance, Sarsa(lambda) temporal updates, checkpoint20/canonical7/WAL14, crash/replay tests, and a reproducible numeric environment. V5/MUSE/BMPS are not initialized or used; production defaults and physical-action authorization remain unchanged.

Five independent seeds, 4,000 training episodes each: trained greedy net return 0.508751 versus validation-selected static3 0.444452; paired delta +0.064300, 95% CI [0.062821,0.065778]. Mean nonstop operations fall from 3 to 1.4859. 336/464 policy parameters change; world synapses are unchanged. Lambda1 does not clearly beat matched TD0.

**Not ready to merge as the completed foundation.** Longer-chain zero-shot transfer fails (-0.034219 versus static5 0.366584). A controlled active-distractor probe has only 50% non-bias credit precision (32 relevant plus 32 irrelevant updates). Reward reversal harms prior behavioral retention. Thus gates C and D fail despite successful code/recovery checks. Native mode also does not yet share the legacy sensor/inquiry pipeline or migrate existing V5 checkpoints.

Local full tests, vet/build, targeted race, process-exit-after-fsync recovery, duplicate-outcome/restart guards, and Android arm64 cross-build passed. A retained 64-episode WAL plus 5-episode suffix reproduces canonical state, activation and checksum. Seed101 was reproduced with identical functional metrics after the final substrate change. Exact-head PR CI 42252885318 and push CI 42252877333 both passed on 0ef994a1d8842b36dbc6b994ecafcb0bf9951174. These technical passes do not change the failed scientific gates.

Performance work was independently merged in #60 as 32df59b9285d829ae73429c7f277621e63de7ce3. Its final ABBA benchmark on 40k/160k gives p95 58.83→23.945 ms (2.46x), allocation bytes -68.54%; the 3x large-workload goal remains unmet. The first allocation optimization regressed latency and was corrected before integration. Sparse lazy kernel is experimental and not always faster when dense.

See docs/research/native_foundation/REPORT.md, PERFORMANCE.md, PROTOCOL.md and JSON results for source audit, root causes, gates, raw-data protocol and reproduction commands. Keep this PR draft while scientific failures remain; do not enable the controller by default.

62.head: research/native-phase2-20261107
62.body:
PR61's operation values are tied to world NodeIDs, so learned behavior fails on new graph addresses and longer chains. This stacked, opt-in continuation shares a four-channel local graph readout through 80 ordinary canonical synapses, adds explicit empirical paired trials with optional factual-mean calibration, and reduces snapshot/readout allocations. One Brain/N and the existing propagate/focus/relax/stop primitives are preserved. Main PR60 is merged into this branch without rewriting PR61; production defaults are unchanged.

Five fresh seeds, 2,500 episodes/model: greedy return is 0.513248 on new samples of the trained distribution. Zero-shot chain 4–5 return improves from the matched per-ID control's −0.106517 to 0.388639; chain 6–7 from −0.050125 to 0.308639. NodeID permutation, new populations, noise and amplitude transfers are reported separately. The encoder is fixed numerical graph moments with a learned projection, not an end-to-end learned representation. After 512 longer-chain experiences, matched old-task retention changes by −0.000203, 95% CI [−0.000768,0.000361]. Hidden reward reversal still destroys retention.

Paired factual trials improve non-bias credit precision from 50% to 100% on the controlled propagate→stop distractor probe, but the initial matched behavioral return is identical. A separate cost-boundary diagnostic exposed calibration failure. On five new confirmation seeds, factual-mean calibration improves the earlier paired candidate (+0.009806, 95% CI [0.003300,0.016311]) but does not beat ordinary learning (−0.001729, CI [−0.004919,0.001462]). Low-data arms still fail. Pair IDs do not certify exogenous matching, and causal labels are never supplied to the learner.

Performance: controller p95 improves 1.43× without WAL / 1.61× with fsync; dense relational readout allocations fall from 120,016 to 16. However, the final isolated legacy whole-thought comparison still regresses p95 about 10% (30.485→33.520 ms), with its cause unresolved. Earlier slower measurements are retained. No 3× whole-thought claim.

Local full regression, targeted race, vet/build, Android arm64 cross-build, numerical credit checks, pending-pair restore, duplicate protection and subprocess crash boundaries pass. A retained checkpoint/WAL suffix reproduces canonical state, activation and checksum at sequence 531. Final seed2027 functional metrics reproduce exactly. Checkpoint20/canonical7/WAL14 containers remain; model v2 is explicit opt-in and older binaries reject it. No physical actions can be replayed by this path.

**Keep draft; do not merge as a completed foundation.** Gate C is only demonstrated within the tested graph family, Gate D has no behavioral superiority, reversal retention fails, and Gate E has an unresolved legacy regression. Production integration Gate G is therefore not passed. PR61 remains independently draft.

Reports, protocols, machine-readable results and reproduction commands: [Phase II report](https://github.com/mpsprintit-spec/horizon-artificial-brain/blob/ea69b2101004dbf10c07068e42436170c2adcf8d/docs/research/native_foundation/phase2/REPORT.md), [performance](https://github.com/mpsprintit-spec/horizon-artificial-brain/blob/ea69b2101004dbf10c07068e42436170c2adcf8d/docs/research/native_foundation/phase2/PERFORMANCE.md), [validation](https://github.com/mpsprintit-spec/horizon-artificial-brain/blob/ea69b2101004dbf10c07068e42436170c2adcf8d/docs/research/native_foundation/phase2/VALIDATION.md).

Published head: `ea69b2101004dbf10c07068e42436170c2adcf8d`, tree `22afd45d51b46ecf2956e988f6a382b8c13826ff`. The repository API merge `2f3038262b2169723356f7ca403a09a08288ffdf` has exactly the same tree as the local `f33b5bb` merge named in the report. The tested local commit `7d46e2151194d9337e85ec23b683bc90061e2583` and published head also have identical trees.

Verification on published head `ea69b2101004dbf10c07068e42436170c2adcf8d`: exact-head [push CI 42440901174](https://github.com/mpsprintit-spec/horizon-artificial-brain/actions/runs/42440901174) **passed**, including full race, Android build, production recovery and Bridge integration; monitor passed. The duplicate [PR CI 42440930780](https://github.com/mpsprintit-spec/horizon-artificial-brain/actions/runs/42440930780) is still running at this update. A fresh local Android arm64 build also passed on this exact tree (cross-build, not on-device execution).

Retained raw evidence: `Horizon_Native_PhaseII_Evidence_20261108.zip`, 55231690 bytes, 369 payload files including 72 checkpoints, original recovery WAL, seed outputs, failing/passing test logs, profiles and benchmark resource records. SHA256: `ced8badd16bf16c73a8c6b97427108739887cc60d26bcba731d44efcc4df7ec2`. The archive's manifest hashes each payload and records both CI statuses. It has been delivered separately to the repository owner. Technical CI success does not change the failed/limited scientific gates or authorize production merge.

63.head: fix/bootstrap-idempotent-startup-android
63.body:
## Root cause
`initializeProductionHorizon` returns a boolean **needsBootstrap**. Production `services/ai/main.go` mistakenly treated it as **loadedBrain** and executed bootstrap on `!loadedBrain`, so recovered checkpoints/journals were given the hardcoded event ID `bootstrap` again. This results in `duplicate event ID "bootstrap"` during Termux startup.

## Fix
- Rename call-site flag to `needsBootstrap`.
- Extract bootstrap-or-resume logic into `finishProductionStartup` so production uses the boolean correctly.
- Preserve canonical journal/checkpoint/memory untouched on recovered start.
- Add regression test exercising actual first-boot → save → close → recover → resume sequence and asserting no extra event, no memory mutation, same neural graph, no duplicate bootstrap.

## User safety
- Do **not** delete checkpoint, `brain_memory.json`, or `horizon_events.jsonl` to fix the error.
- Does not alter `horizon-mobile` or the canonical neural substrate implementation.

## Validation
Awaiting CI. Branch intentionally separate from `main` until checked.

64.head: research/native-phase3-20261108
64.body:
Phase II feature contrasts improved attribution on a probe without improving decisions. This research continuation adds explicit matched factual **action** contrasts: two executed trials share their initial neural state and declared matching scope, differ in the first operation, and use a controlled continuation with absorbing stop. Observed return differences, including all executed costs, train operation advantages through the existing canonical synapses. No second Brain/weight store, V5 dependency or production-default controller change.

Two preregistered five-seed confirmations use 2,048 factual training episodes and 512 greedy cases per model. With shared nuisance reward offsets, return is 0.097977 versus unpaired −0.269596 (paired gain +0.367572, CI95 [0.065095,0.670049]); delayed depths 0–2 give 0.085684 versus −0.452912 (gain +0.538595, CI95 [0.470252,0.606938]). Clean controls nearly tie; deliberately unmatched pairs degrade performance. All scoped registered numerical criteria pass. Assigned intervention training is distinguished from greedy evaluation.

**This remains draft.** Learned-effect precision/recall is 100% on the controlled probe, but exclusive first-pair synaptic precision remains 50% (8 relevant and 8 nuisance updates). Gate D is therefore incomplete. An executed excitatory/inhibitory counterexample proves a collision in the fixed four-moment encoder; broader Gate C and observable-context retention Gate H remain open. Real sensor/inquiry/continuous coexistence Gate G is not enabled.

Native command preflight now uses isolated metadata without cloning full episodes; digests and checkpoint APIs are unchanged. Exact frozen-model reproduction matches behavior, Brain, activation, checksum and sequence. Dense-pair allocated bytes fall about 14.47%; dense execution and JSON restore remain expensive. Conservative curiosity allocation repair was independently merged to main via [PR65](https://github.com/mpsprintit-spec/horizon-artificial-brain/pull/65), then merged into this branch without rewriting PR61/62. Its matched main ABBA thought p95 improves 24.720→12.255ms (2.017×), allocated bytes fall 97.04%; no cross-host multiplication or 3× claim.

Validation: final local full regression, targeted native/race/curiosity suite, vet/build, Android arm64 native+chat builds pass. Version3 retained pending-pair checkpoint/WAL suffix replay reproduces canonical state, activation and checksum through sequence531, with zero physical actions. Crash, duplicate and mismatch rejection tests pass; old Phase II binary explicitly rejects modelv3. Final-head CI is running: [42567905600](https://github.com/mpsprintit-spec/horizon-artificial-brain/actions/runs/42567905600). Previous exact-head e8a59cf CI and PR65 CI passed full race, nested adapters, trained-dialogue/production recovery, Android, Bridge and monitor.

Source HEAD `0df3f19a33bd7de69ed496293591d734331c5e51`, tree `202981711c5e662506c0331ee84b1b9177a34631`, exactly equal to tested local tree. Code unit `e3a105818dccad051b2f0f2b3c78c5de6bfeb0c0`; merge parent main `45ecb989b67da690b9bbc1b7a942bb8c55ca6f8e`. PR remains stacked on PR62 `ea69b21`.

65.head: perf/stream-curiosity-selection-20261108
65.body:
Every autonomous thought currently allocates and stable-sorts the entire curiosity candidate population even though only the winner is used. Select the same maximum in one pass through the existing canonical address visitor, retaining the score, lowest-ID tie break, heartbeat and write boundary. Preserve the historical fallback for nonfinite in-memory scores. No neural law, checkpoint schema, native-controller default or learned parameter changes.

A 512-case numerical comparison against the old implementation covers ties, clamping, negative frequency, growth and NaN ordering. Local full regression, targeted concurrency/race tests, vet and Android arm64 cross-build pass. Exact-head CI [42497869614](https://github.com/mpsprintit-spec/horizon-artificial-brain/actions/runs/42497869614) passed full race, nested adapter validation, trained dialogue/recovery, Android build, live Bridge smoke and monitor checks. Merged as `45ecb989b67da690b9bbc1b7a942bb8c55ca6f8e`.

Matched sequential ABBA on PR60 main versus this change, same Go1.23.2/GOMAXPROCS1/GOGC100 environment, 40k neurons/160k synapses, 200 iterations/run: thought p95 24.720→12.255ms (2.017x), p50 10.385→9.6475ms, p99 33.590→14.575ms. Sensor+thought allocations 3,855,267.5→114,244.5B/op (−97.04%); GC cycles during measured intervals 13→0. Means of per-run statistics, not pooled percentiles or confidence intervals. Production GC settings remain unchanged. No 3x or on-device Android claim.

This conservative optimization is deliberately independent of experimental PR61/62/64. The native learning foundations remain draft with incomplete scientific gates. Details and raw primary measurements: services/ai/runtime/CURIOSITY_SELECTION_PERFORMANCE.md.
